gen-gf-noto-serif-gurmukhi-fs-asap: Noto Serif Gurmukhi has a bookish, traditional look, its strokes only lightly modulated and its capitals nearly as short as its lowercase. Asap follows in sans-serif, with open arcs on its c and a body height close to the capitals.
gen-gf-noto-serif-gurmukhi-fs-epilogue: Epilogue reads as curvy and loose, a tall-bodied lowercase with stubby ascender tips and a wire-like skeleton of single-width strokes. Noto Serif Gurmukhi sits against it, quieter and more traditional.
gen-gf-noto-serif-gurmukhi-fs-fira-sans: Clean and sturdy, Fira Sans opens its s curves wide at both ends and carries a larger-than-usual x-height with no stroke variation. Noto Serif Gurmukhi handles the bookish, medium-contrast voice; Fira Sans handles the plain work.
gen-gf-noto-serif-gurmukhi-fs-public-san: Public Sans reads hefty and trustworthy, its lowercase solid and its counters on c and s broad and open. Noto Serif Gurmukhi above it tapers modestly, so a long passage feels weighty but easy to move through.
gen-gf-noto-serif-gurmukhi-fs-supreme: Supreme lays down a thick, heavy-looking band of text, crisp, with letters that feel held open rather than curled shut. Noto Serif Gurmukhi does the fine, glass-etched shifts in weight; Supreme does the sturdy, steady lines.
gen-gf-noto-serif-gurmukhi-general-sans: Traditional and bookish at the top. General Sans takes over below with steady pressure, an x-height filling the line, and bowls that curve smoothly without thinning, a plain sans against the lightly flexed contrast of Noto Serif Gurmukhi.
gen-gf-noto-serif-gurmukhi-montserrat: Montserrat arrives geometric and generous with space. Noto Serif Gurmukhi brings a small, steady shift in stroke thickness, while Montserrat's oversized e and a counters and hairline-free curves glide beneath it like wire, and that gap between them is the pair's real draw.
gen-gf-noto-serif-gurmukhi-satoshi: Noto Serif Gurmukhi leads with a modest weight shift inside each stroke, traditional and bookish. Satoshi follows with a soaring x-height and a wide-open e, each stroke cut to one width, so a longer stretch of it reads smooth and unhurried.
gen-gf-noto-serif-gurmukhi-switzer: Switzer reads in tubular, wire-like letterforms, with a tall waist line and c tips that never drift toward touching. Noto Serif Gurmukhi gives gentle weight shifts in its bowls; Switzer holds a drafting-pen line.
gen-gf-noto-serif-gurmukhi-work-sans: Bookish meets modern here, the light modulation of Noto Serif Gurmukhi set against Work Sans, whose tails and terminals are as thick as its stems. Work Sans holds a high mean line and open c tips beneath it.
